ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening must be conducted against UN Security Council Consolidated Lists, OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists, EU consolidated sanctions lists, HKAMLO Schedule 2 designated persons, PRC Ministry of Public Security sanctions and wanted lists, and global PEP databases (including family members and close associates), for all shareholders, directors, UBOs, signatories, and beneficial owners. Screening must occur at onboarding, prior to incorporation, and continuously during the business relationship using automated name-matching with fuzzy logic and adverse media review. Any positive hit triggers enhanced due diligence, source-of-funds verification, senior management approval, and reporting to the HK Joint Financial Intelligence Unit or PRC competent authority where required. The EdTech subscription business is low-risk but the dual HK/PRC structure requires segregated PEP and sanctions declarations, with UBO register maintained and available for government inspection under PBOC/SAMR Order No. 3.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Hong Kong Companies Registry e-Registry (Cyber Search Centre); PRC SAMR National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System (NECIPS) for WFOE name clearance
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A Hong Kong company may adopt an English name, a Chinese name, or both. The English name must consist of roman letters; the Chinese name must use traditional Chinese characters and may not be a phonetic transliteration of the English name unless it complies with Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) s. 8. For the PRC WFOE, the Chinese name must follow the four-tier SAMR convention: administrative division + distinctive name + industry characteristic + company form (limited liability company). Transliteration between Hong Kong and WFOE names must be visually distinctive and not conflict with a pre-existing registered name in SAMR. The HK Chinese name and the PRC Chinese name may differ as long as the UBO structure is documented.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Education (where implying regulated educational institution without license)
China (as a standalone token requiring special approval)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection by HK Companies Registry, the applicant must file a written appeal to the Registrar of Companies within 14 days, referencing the proposed name, the statutory basis for distinctiveness, a revised name or supporting trademark/search evidence, and the original application reference. The Registrar will issue a final determination; an unsuccessful appeal can be challenged by judicial review. For a PRC SAMR rejection, an administrative reconsideration must be filed with the local market regulation bureau within 60 days of the rejection decision; if reconsideration fails, an administrative lawsuit may be filed within 6 months to the competent people's court. To preserve the 30-day reservation window, immediately re-file with an alternative name and simultaneously appeal the original refusal. Maintain a name-rejection log to demonstrate good-faith clearance for the post-incorporation compliance file.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Rejected for this industry and entity structure. A Hong Kong private limited company must have a physical registered office in Hong Kong under Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) s. 657, which cannot be a P.O. box, but may be a licensed serviced office or corporate service provider address only if the provider has a physical front desk and mail handling. For the PRC WFOE, the SAMR requires a registered domicile that is the principal place of business under PRC Company Law Art. 10; virtual offices or commercial mailbox addresses will be rejected by local SAMR and tax authorities for EdTech subscription companies because of the need for physical inspection, VAT registration, onsite contracts, and bank relationship verification. PRC tax authorities require an actual lease contract, and banks under PBOC AML rules will reject a purely virtual address. A serviced office with a physical suite, dedicated signage, full-time staff, and utility bills may be acceptable if the bank and tax bureau accept it in writing.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) SAMR unannounced inspection of registered address within 12-24 months of incorporation—high likelihood; (2) local tax bureau on-site visit triggered by abnormal VAT filings or zero-turnover—moderate; (3) HK Companies Registry address verification on complaint or annual return audit—moderate; (4) HK Inland Revenue Department field audit if business profits/losses inconsistent with subscription model—moderate; (5) bank pre-account-opening site visit—certain before account approval; (6) unannounced physical inspection probability quantified as High for the PRC WFOE (estimated >50% in first 3 years) and Moderate for the Hong Kong holding entity (estimated 20-30%). Mitigation: maintain permanent lease, physical signage, staff presence, complete utility records, and a local sublease or shared-office access log.

incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Establishment of a Foreign-Invested Enterprise (Form A) and Articles of Association
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. Under the Foreign Investment Law, there is no statutory minimum paid-up capital for a WFOE. However, the registered capital must be subscribed in the Articles of Association and paid in within the time period specified therein (typically within 30 years for service companies). The capital must be injected into a designated capital contribution account in the company's bank. No escrow account is required, but the capital must be verifiable and traceable.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLVED, that the incorporation of the Company as a wholly foreign-owned enterprise under the laws of the People's Republic of China is hereby approved, and the Articles of Association as presented to this meeting are adopted as the governing instrument of the Company.

RESOLVED FURTHER, that the share capital of the Company, as set forth in the Articles of Association, is hereby subscribed in full by the sole shareholder, and the directors are authorized to take all necessary steps to effect the payment of such capital into the Company's designated capital contribution account.

RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office of the Company shall be at [address], and the directors are hereby authorized to execute any lease or other agreements necessary to secure such premises.

RESOLVED FURTHER, that the following persons are hereby appointed to the statutory offices of the Company: [Name] as Director and Legal Representative, [Name] as Supervisor, and [Name] as General Manager, each to serve until their successors are duly appointed.

RESOLVED FURTHER, that the directors are authorized to open and maintain bank accounts in the name of the Company with any bank or financial institution, and to appoint such signatories as they deem appropriate, with the power to bind the Company and execute banking transactions.

RESOLVED FURTHER, that the directors are authorized to engage legal counsel, auditors, and other professional advisors as necessary to complete the incorporation and registration of the Company, and to execute all documents and forms required by the State Administration for Market Regulation and other government authorities.

RESOLVED FURTHER, that the directors are authorized to take all actions necessary to obtain any business licenses, permits, or approvals required for the Company's operations, including but not limited to tax registration, social insurance registration, and any industry-specific licenses.

RESOLVED FURTHER, that the directors are authorized to adopt a corporate seal and to use such seal in the execution of all corporate documents.

RESOLVED FURTHER, that the directors are authorized to delegate any of the foregoing powers to any officer or agent of the Company as they deem appropriate.

RESOLVED FURTHER, that all actions taken by the directors prior to this meeting in connection with the incorporation of the Company are hereby ratified and confirmed.

RESOLVED FURTHER, that this resolution shall be effective immediately and shall remain in full force until revoked or amended by a subsequent resolution of the Board of Directors.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) – Online Name Reservation System (via the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation application through the SAMR online portal, providing the proposed company name in Chinese and English, the intended business scope, and the registered capital amount. The name must comply with the national regulations on enterprise name registration. The application must be submitted by the sole shareholder or an authorized representative. Upon approval, a Name Reservation Notice will be issued, valid for six months. Ensure that the name does not conflict with existing trademarks or registered enterprises. The submission should include the shareholder's identification documents and a power of attorney if applicable. The process is entirely electronic and requires a verified digital signature.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected due to similarity, the applicant may amend the name and resubmit. If the rejection is based on a conflict, provide evidence of distinctiveness or obtain a letter of consent from the conflicting entity. If the system flags a technical issue, contact SAMR support or engage a local agent.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Notarization of Incorporation Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public Office (for notarization) and the local SAMR office (for filing)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Association, the Application for Establishment, and other required documents. The Articles must be notarized by a Chinese notary public. The lease agreement for the registered office must also be notarized. All documents must be in Chinese or accompanied by a certified Chinese translation. The shareholder's identity documents must be notarized and legalized (apostille) if originating from a foreign jurisdiction. The registered capital amount and payment schedule must be clearly stated. The appointment of the legal representative, supervisor, and manager must be documented. After notarization, the documents are ready for submission to SAMR.
required_dossiers: Notarized lease agreement for registered office
Notarized and legalized shareholder identity documents
Appointment documents for legal representative, supervisor, and manager
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If notarization is delayed, engage a local notary service experienced with foreign investors. If documents are rejected, correct the deficiencies and re-notarize. If legalization is required, ensure the apostille process is completed in the shareholder's home country.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission to SAMR for Business License
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) – Enterprise Registration Office (or online via the National Enterprise Service Portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the complete set of notarized documents to the SAMR office with jurisdiction over the registered address. The application must be filed by the legal representative or an authorized agent. SAMR will review the documents for compliance with the Company Law and Foreign Investment Law. Upon approval, SAMR will issue the Business License (营业执照) and the company is officially incorporated. The license includes the unified social credit code. The process typically takes 5-10 working days. After issuance, the company must register for tax, social insurance, and other statutory obligations.
required_dossiers: Proof of payment of registration fee (if any)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SAMR issues a query, respond within the given timeframe with additional explanations or documents. If the application is suspended, seek legal counsel to address the specific issues. If the license is denied, appeal through the administrative reconsideration process.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Registrations and Bank Account Opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Tax Bureau (State Taxation Administration), Social Insurance Bureau, Public Security Bureau (for seal carving), and a commercial bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After obtaining the business license, complete tax registration with the local tax authority within 30 days, obtain a tax identification number, and register for value-added tax and corporate income tax. Social insurance registration must be completed within 30 days. The company must also carve a company seal, financial seal, and legal representative seal at a licensed seal engraving company. Open a corporate bank account with a commercial bank, providing the business license, seals, and identification of the legal representative. The bank will conduct due diligence and may require a minimum deposit. The capital contribution must be deposited into the account within the specified period.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax registration is delayed, contact the tax bureau to expedite and pay any penalties. If social insurance registration is delayed, apply for an extension. If bank account opening is delayed, provide additional documentation or choose another bank. If seal carving is delayed, use a certified seal maker.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) of the People's Republic of China; all tax registrations, filings, and VAT/export treatment applications for the PRC-incorporated WFOE are processed through the provincial Electronic Tax Bureau (e-Tax) portal and the national Fully Digitalized Electronic Invoice platform. The Hong Kong Inland Revenue Department is not a registration authority for the WFOE itself, but Hong Kong tax obligations, if any, arise only at the shareholder level.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Chinese WFOE obtains its statutory tax identification number automatically from the 18-digit Unified Social Credit Code (USCC) printed on its business license issued by the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR). Within 30 days of incorporation, the WFOE must activate the USCC as its taxpayer identification number in the e-Tax Bureau, register its legal representative, financial officer, and tax accountant, confirm VAT taxpayer status (small-scale or general VAT taxpayer), file bank account details, and enrol in the electronic invoice service platform. A foreign non-resident entity without a permanent establishment in China that receives China-source income must obtain a non-resident taxpayer identification number through the withholding agent by submitting the non-resident tax registration and treaty benefit paperwork in the e-Tax Bureau; no Chinese business license is required for that non-resident registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None - China does not provide a US-style check-the-box election or a hybrid mismatch election. A WFOE is automatically a Chinese resident enterprise subject to enterprise income tax at 25% on worldwide income. For VAT only, a taxpayer with annual taxable sales not exceeding CNY 5,000,000 may elect simplified small-scale taxpayer treatment at 3% (temporarily 1% during relief windows), while a taxpayer exceeding that threshold must register as a general VAT taxpayer; small-scale taxpayers may voluntarily opt into general VAT taxpayer status. The WFOE may also elect cross-border service zero-rating or exemption treatment if the statutory export substance requirements are satisfied.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: An entity engaged in taxable transactions must register for VAT within 30 days of obtaining its business licence. Mandatory registration as a general VAT taxpayer is triggered when cumulative annual taxable sales exceed CNY 5,000,000. The WFOE's EdTech subscription and software services are generally subject to the 6% modern-services VAT rate, while domestic sales of physical goods, if any, are subject to the 13% goods headline rate.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: The WFOE must issue Fully Digitalized Electronic Invoices (FDEI) through the STA's national Electronic Invoice Service Platform. Each invoice is assigned a unique tax-control invoice number and authenticated in real time by the Golden Tax IV system, with a digital stamp and electronic delivery to the buyer. Invoice issuance is quota-controlled and monitored by invoice amount, item type, and counterparty risk classification. ERP-connected taxpayers may use the platform's APIs for automated invoice creation, delivery, and status retrieval. All invoice data is pushed to the tax authority immediately upon issuance, and traditional tax-control disk and paper invoice processes are being phased out.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero per cent VAT applies to (1) physical exports of goods that are actually exported from China and recorded by Customs, and (2) cross-border supplies of software services to overseas customers where the services are wholly consumed outside China, the overseas recipient is the contracting party, the services are not supplied to a Chinese resident or connected with domestic goods, labour, or real estate, and payment is received in foreign currency from outside China. For the EdTech subscription software, the WFOE must demonstrate offshore use through overseas IP addresses, server logs, user geography, and platform session data, and the sale must qualify as a cross-border taxable service under the VAT zero-rating/exemption rules for software services, information system services, and business process services.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Bill of Entry) with verified customs release record, for physical goods exports
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing transport of goods out of China, for physical goods exports
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or SAFE bank foreign-exchange receipt voucher evidencing collection and settlement of export proceeds
Cross-border service agreement identifying the overseas entity, service scope, and consideration, for digital EdTech subscription sales

Offshore consumption evidence, including overseas IP addresses, server logs, device and user location data, and platform session records, together with the e-Tax zero-rating/exemption filing reference for cross-border services
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Tax authorities will require the full export documentation bundle before approving zero-rating or an export VAT refund. If zero-rating is claimed without actual export, without offshore consumption of digital services, without foreign exchange repatriation within the prescribed period, or with forged documentation, the tax authority will reverse the zero-rating, recover the underpaid VAT plus daily late-payment interest, and impose a monetary penalty of 50% to 500% of the tax under the Tax Collection Administration Law. Fraudulent refunds, false export declarations, and false VAT special invoices are criminal offences under the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China and the Customs Law of the People's Republic of China, with no limitation period for recovery in tax fraud cases and personal criminal liability for the legal representative and responsible officers.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) of the People's Republic of China, operating under the People's Bank of China (PBOC)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: China's RMB is convertible on the current account: fees for software licensing, app store commission, and employee-related service payments can be settled through domestic banks with supporting documentation, without SAFE quota approval. The capital account remains restricted: FDI equity injections into a WFOE require prior SAFE registration, a dedicated Foreign Exchange Capital Account, and bank-level authenticity checks before conversion into RMB. Once converted, RMB must be used for permitted business expenses and enterprise operations; it may not be directed to securities or entrusted loans without additional qualifications. Profit remittance to the Hong Kong parent is permitted as a current-account dividend distribution after annual audit, but the remitting bank must verify audited financial statements, tax payment proof, board resolution, the SAFE registration, and a legal-person payout signature. The practical hurdle is not a fixed cap; it is documentary consistency. Any mismatch in invoice description, customs data, or FX purpose code can freeze the payment for additional due diligence. No exchange control approval is needed for bona fide profits, but the trail from registered business scope to signed agreements and tax records must be immaculate.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under SAFE's current framework, there is no fixed statutory mandatory conversion ratio; however, 100% of export proceeds from goods and services must be repatriated into a domestic foreign exchange account. The bank expects settlement (conversion to RMB) within 30 days after the credit date in the absence of a qualifying retention; any retained foreign exchange balance must be justified by future current-account obligations and must remain within the enterprise's registered current-account quota. Proceeds must be credited no later than 30 days after the underlying customs declaration date or invoice due date, and each receipt must be matched in the Trade Monitoring System before it can be used.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Foreign Exchange Capital Account for FDI capital injection; RMB Basic Operational Current Account for business settlement

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Foreign Exchange Capital Account for FDI capital injection; RMB Basic Operational Current Account for business settlement
Foreign Exchange Capital Account for FDI capital injection; RMB Basic Operational Current Account for business settlement

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Standalone offshore digital EMI platforms, including major cross-border online business account providers, are not legally permitted to open domestic RMB corporate accounts or to access China's CIPS clearing system directly. They are neither licensed deposit-taking institutions nor SAFE-designated foreign exchange banks in mainland China. The WFOE should not use an offshore EMI as its primary treasury rail. At most, the Hong Kong parent may maintain an EMI account for low-value ancillary receipts or contractor payments outside China, but all RMB liquidity, FDI conversion, dividend remittance, and tax-related payments must flow through a domestically licensed tier-1 commercial bank with SAFE qualifications.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The statutory legal representative of the WFOE, who must be a natural person registered on the Chinese business license, is required to appear physically in-branch for the initial KYC interview and for the activation of the Foreign Exchange Capital Account. Remote video KYC is not accepted as a substitute for the first capital-account opening, and consular proxy opening is not permitted. Other directors and shareholders may be onboarded through notarized board resolutions, corporate registry extracts, and apostilled identity documents, but the first compliance interview must be conducted in person at the chosen domestic bank branch before any cross-border funds are received.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership chain terminating at an intermediary entity in Hong Kong, a Cayman holding company, or any trust structure that obscures the natural person ultimate beneficial owners; Chinese banks apply strict look-through requirements under PBOC and SAFE anti-money laundering rules.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete ownership tree from the WFOE up to every individual natural person with more than 25% economic interest; Hong Kong Business Registry extracts; Cayman register of directors and members, if applicable; certificates of incorporation; constitutional documents; notarized and apostilled director/shareholder registers; valid passport or national ID copies of all ultimate beneficial owners; a written source-of-wealth statement covering the funds used for the FDI capital injection; all documents translated into Chinese by a licensed translator and certified by the bank's compliance team.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between the declared EdTech subscription business and actual Apple IAP / Google Play Billing settlement flows; banks may suspect false service trade or disguised cross-border forex settlement if revenue wiring does not match the invoices.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed Apple Developer Program agreement and Google Play Console distribution agreement; app store payout statements showing gross billings, Apple/Google commission, taxes, and net remittances; corresponding tax invoices or self-issued e-fapiao records; server access logs proving the mainland user base; PRC website and mobile app ICP filing; PIPL compliance documentation for the EdTech platform; and a narrative business-flow diagram mapping each subscription payment from the consumer payment rail through the app store payout to the corporate bank account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: FDI capital injection amount disproportionate to operational needs, or funds that appear designed to return to Hong Kong shortly after conversion into RMB; banks may escalate for anti-round-tripping review under SAFE Circular 19 and related anti-circumvention rules.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A prospective 12-month cash-flow budget and treasury projection; lease agreement for the mainland office; payroll headcount plan with social insurance enrollment estimates; signed technology licensing contracts; app store registration certificates; an explanation of the company's actual working-capital requirements; SAFE Foreign Exchange Business Registration Form with the declared investment amount; and an undertaking that converted RMB will not be used for prohibited investments such as entrusted loans, wealth management products, real estate acquisition outside business scope, or outbound guarantees.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border payment chain touching sanctioned jurisdictions, politically exposed persons, or unverified third-party payers in the app-store settlement chain; Chinese banks routinely screen every correspondent and beneficiary against sanctions, PEP, and negative-news lists.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions and PEP screening reports for all directors, shareholders, ultimate beneficial owners, authorized signatories, and material counterparties, generated from an internationally recognized compliance database such as Dow Jones or World-Check; export-control self-certification; confirmation that the EdTech platform blocks access from comprehensively sanctioned countries and that no sanctioned person receives commercial benefit; a list of all third-party payment processors with their license numbers; and a written indemnity undertaking to the bank regarding sanctions compliance.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The Hong Kong parent must remit the registered FDI capital via SWIFT MT103 to the WFOE's designated Foreign Exchange Capital Account at the chosen mainland tier-1 bank. The remittance field must specify 'FDI Capital Injection' and include the SAFE Foreign Exchange Business Registration number; the purpose code must match the registered investment category for software development and EdTech subscription services. Upon receipt, the onshore bank will perform electronic capital verification with SAFE, convert the foreign currency into RMB at the spot rate through the interbank market, and credit the converted funds to a RMB capital settlement account. Drawdown from that account is monitored against the negative list and permitted business expenses. Any excess remittance above the registered amount must be returned by the same SWIFT rail, and a statutory capital verification report prepared by a Chinese certified public accountant should be filed within 30 days after receipt.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For service-trade obligations such as software royalties, technology licensing fees, management fees, cross-border marketing costs, and purchases of cloud infrastructure, the WFOE should use SWIFT MT103 current-account remittances with full supporting contracts, tax payment certificates, and the correct SAFE service-trade purpose code. For physical goods procurement, documentary collections or commercial letters of credit can be used through the advising bank in Hong Kong, with the WFOE as importer and the overseas seller as beneficiary; sight and usance LC structures are acceptable. For routine app-store disbursements from Apple and Google to the WFOE, the platform payout rail is used as the initial settlement channel, and subsequent conversion or repatriation to mainland China must be reported as trade-in-service foreign exchange receipts with the corresponding app-store payout statements. All outbound instructions must be pre-registered with the bank's international settlement system and matched against an approved foreign exchange payment list.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore plain-vanilla RMB forward contracts (Sale and Purchase of Foreign Exchange Against RMB) for genuine current-account receipts and payments with a matching underlying trade document.
Onshore cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCS) and foreign exchange swaps where the notional amount, maturity, and cash flows exactly match the approved capital and current-account exposure.
Onshore FX option strategies, including zero-cost collars and risk reversals, provided the bank confirms the underlying trade exposure and the contracts are not entered for speculative purposes.

Offshore CNH non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not directly permissible for the onshore WFOE; the Hong Kong parent may separately transact CNH NDFs in its own treasury capacity only with independent documentation and without creating a repatriation obligation on the mainland entity.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Hong Kong Annual Return (NAR1) under the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 42 days after the anniversary date of incorporation each year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fees range from HK$600 (more than 42 days up to 3 months) to HK$900 (3-6 months), HK$1,200 (6-12 months) and HK$3,000 (over 12 months). The company and its officers may be prosecuted, and the company may be struck off the Companies Register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Business Registration Certificate renewal fee payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Hong Kong Inland Revenue Department, Business Registration Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the expiry date shown on the current Business Registration Certificate, normally on the annual registration anniversary.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A late renewal incurs a HK$300 additional charge, prosecution under the Business Registration Ordinance, recovery of outstanding fees as a tax debt, and possible cancellation or striking off of the business registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Hong Kong Profits Tax Return (BIR51) with audited financial statements and tax computation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month of issue date; with a tax representative for a 31 December accounting period, generally extended to 15 November of the following year; for a 31 March accounting period, generally extended to 15 August.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The Inland Revenue Department may issue default assessments and impose penalties of HK$2,000 to HK$50,000; additional tax of up to three times the tax undercharged may be levied.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Hong Kong Employer's Return (BIR56A and supplementary employer forms)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month of issue, generally issued in early April each year for the preceding year of assessment.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines up to HK$10,000 and prosecution; the Inland Revenue Department may raise best-of-judgment assessments against the employer.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: China WFOE annual report to SAMR, combined with the Foreign Investment Information Report to MOFCOM
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) and Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) via the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System (NECIPS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 1 January to 30 June each year for the preceding fiscal year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to report results in inclusion on the list of enterprises with abnormal operations; continuation for three years triggers the serious illegal and dishonest list, fines of RMB 10,000-RMB 30,000, and credit restrictions on the legal representative.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: China Annual Corporate Income Tax Final Settlement and filing of annual financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local State Taxation Administration having jurisdiction over the WFOE
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 5 months after calendar year-end, i.e., by 31 May of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment interest at 0.05% per day; late filing fines up to RMB 10,000; penalties of 50%-500% of underpaid tax; tax collection measures including bank account freezing and exit restrictions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Certified annual financial statement audit report of the China WFOE
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: SAMR/MOFCOM joint annual reporting platform and local tax authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: CICPA audit completion and submission of audited financial statements by 31 May for tax final settlement and by 30 June for the annual report.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to submit an audit report may invalidate the annual report, trigger abnormal-listing status, and result in tax documentation penalties and disallowance of deductions.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Hong Kong: a private company must be audited unless it qualifies as a small private company by satisfying at least two of the following: total revenue not exceeding HK$10,000,000; total assets not exceeding HK$10,000,000; employees not exceeding 50; and no eligible member has requested an audit. China WFOE: a PRC CICPA audit is mandatory for all foreign-invested enterprises regardless of revenue, total assets or headcount; listed companies, banks, insurers, securities intermediaries and state-owned or state-controlled enterprises are also compulsorily audited under PRC law and regulatory requirements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: China: PRC Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (ASBEs), substantially converged with IFRS, with PRC Small Enterprise Accounting Standards available to qualifying small enterprises. Hong Kong: HKFRS/IFRS for the holding company, with HKFRS for Private Entities or SME-FRS available to eligible private companies.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Hong Kong: no annual UBO filing is made to the Companies Registry; a Significant Controllers Register must be maintained on-site and updated within 7 days of any change, for inspection by law enforcement. China WFOE: the annual Foreign Investment Information Report, filed by 30 June, must disclose ultimate beneficial ownership; any shareholding or UBO change must be reported to SAMR within 30 days of the registration change. Annual general meetings are not statutorily required in Hong Kong unless the articles so require.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 400 - USD 2,500 per entity per year; combined Hong Kong registered agent/corporate secretary and China registered office services typically USD 700 - USD 4,500.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,500 - USD 3,500 for the China WFOE; USD 1,000 - USD 2,500 for the Hong Kong holding; combined annual certified audit typically USD 2,500 - USD 6,000.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Preferential 15% rate for High-and-New Technology Enterprises (HNTE) in the EdTech software sector; Small Low-Profit Enterprise concession regime effectively reduces EIT on qualifying annual taxable income up to RMB 3 million to approximately 5%; R&D expenses eligible for an additional 100% super-deduction from taxable income; certain software development and licensing enterprises may qualify for the 'two-year exemption and three-year 50% reduction' policy on enterprise income tax; free-trade-zone (e.g., Hainan FTP, Qianhai) and regional incentives may apply only where genuine economic substance is established and statutory conditions are met.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: PRC Enterprise Income Tax Annual Return (Form A) (EIT File A100000) together with applicable supporting schedules; filed electronically through the State Taxation Administration's e-Tax Bureau (electronic tax declaration system).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual settlement complemented by quarterly provisional (prepayment) filings during the fiscal year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a calendar-year WFOE, the annual EIT return must be filed within 5 months after fiscal year-end (i.e., by 31 May of the subsequent year). Quarterly provisional returns must be filed within 15 days after the end of each calendar quarter. Any dividend withholding tax must be remitted within 15 days of the actual dividend distribution.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating revenue (营业收入) — total gross revenue from EdTech language-learning subscriptions, Apple App Store / Google Play in-app purchases, institutional training fees, and licensing income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all gross revenue sourced in and outside China; do not net out platform commissions or payment processing fees (these are expenses in Box 2). For revenue attributable to non-resident related parties, ensure the amount is at arm's length and properly identified in the related-party transaction disclosure schedules. In-app purchase flows via Apple or Google should be fully recognised in Chinese accounts, with the platform commission supported by valid VAT/FTT invoices.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating expense (营业成本) — direct costs of delivering the online language education service, including software development, server hosting, teacher compensation, content creation, royalties, and platform fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border royalties paid to a Hong Kong parent for proprietary language-learning software or content are deductible only if the payment is bona fide, arm's length, and beneficiated by actual IP. Deductibility additionally requires satisfaction of the 7% treaty withholding tax documentation, or the statutory 10% withholding tax where treaty relief is unavailable. Related-party management fees must satisfy the Economic Substance Doctrine and be backed by actual services, not passive allocations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total accounting profit (利润总额) — the standalone financial statement profit calculated under China Accounting Standards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This figure must reflect the WFOE's own functional and risk profile. Do not consolidate with the Hong Kong parent's financial statements. Any transfer pricing adjustments to revenue or expense are made subsequently in Boxes 4 and 5, not directly in this Box. Ensure all related-party transactions are disclosed to permit the tax authority to test economic substance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax adjustment additions (纳税调整增加额) — items that increase taxable income: non-deductible entertainment expenses, excess advertising expenses, non-arm's-length related-party charges, excessive interest deductions, and other permanent/temporary differences.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back disallowed intercompany royalties or management fees paid to the Hong Kong parent where the WFOE cannot prove actual benefit, arm's-length pricing, or economic substance. Also add back interest deductions exceeding the arm's-length debt/equity ratio under the thin capitalisation rule. If the Hong Kong parent is a shell or conduit, the tax authority may recharacterise a portion of the royalty as a deemed distribution taxable as a dividend.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax adjustment deductions (纳税调整减少额) — items that reduce taxable income: tax-exempt dividends received, R&D super-deductions, additional deductions for disabled employee wages, and carry-forward realisation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Qualifying R&D expenses incurred in developing the WFOE's EdTech platform may be deducted at 100% additional deduction (i.e., 200% total deduction) subject to the R&D project filing. Tax-exempt investment income from a resident subsidiary, if any, is excluded. Do not deduct exclusions or exemptions available only to the Hong Kong parent; treaty reductions are addressed at the withholding layer, not in the EIT return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Loss carryforward offset (弥补以前年度亏损) — current-year taxable income offset by prior-year unrelieved tax losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For ordinary WFOEs, the carryforward period is 5 years from the loss year. If the WFOE qualifies as a High-and-New Technology Enterprise, an extended 10-year carryforward may apply. Losses cannot be transferred to the Hong Kong parent; separate tax-loss computation under Chinese rules is mandatory. A WFOE cannot offset a loss against the foreign investor's income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income (应纳税所得额) — amount after Box 4 additions and Box 5 reductions, then applying the Box 6 loss offset.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This is the final base for EIT. It must reconcile with the audited financial statements and the transfer pricing report. If the tax authority has made a TP adjustment in prior years, such adjustment is reflected here consistently with the final assessment. Cross-border digital service revenue must be sourced under Chinese PE/deemed source rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: EIT payable before reductions and credits (应纳所得税额) — taxable income multiplied by the applicable statutory or preferential CIT rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use 25% statutory rate for the WFOE, or 15% if the WFOE is approved as an HNTE. For qualifying Small Low-Profit Enterprises, apply the applicable reduced rate formula. No credit is allowed for WHT that will be withheld on future distributions of profit; that is a shareholder-level tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax reduction and exemption amounts (减免所得税额) — preferential reductions such as HNTE rate differential, small-enterprise concessions, and regional tax incentives.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any claimed incentive must be evidenced by an approved qualification certificate or self-filing record, e.g., HNTE certificate, software enterprise filing, or free-zone registration. The WFOE must maintain contemporaneous documentation of the eligibility and economic substance of the activity. If a preferential rate is improperly claimed, the entire differential is recoverable with 0.05% daily late surcharge and penalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits (抵免所得税额) — foreign tax credits on overseas sourced income that is taxed in China, and equipment/energy-saving credits where applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the WFOE derives income from a permanent establishment abroad, credit must be computed globally under the PRC foreign tax credit rules, limited to China EIT attributable to the foreign-sourced income. For an EdTech WFOE, most foreign revenue is sourced in China, so foreign tax credits are rarely applicable. Do not claim credits for amounts withheld in Hong Kong on dividends from China; that is not a foreign tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Actual EIT payable for the year (实际应纳所得税额) — Box 8 minus Box 9 and Box 10, net of quarterly prepayments, producing the final settled tax liability or refund.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: After the EIT return is settled and any refund is applied, the remaining distributable profit (including accumulated retained earnings) may be distributed. At the time of distribution, the WFOE as withholding agent must withhold Chinese dividend WHT at 10% (or 5% under the China-HK DTA if treaty conditions and TRC are met) and remit the WHT within 15 days. No EIT credit is available against this downstream withholding.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.failure_penalties: Late filing of the annual EIT return attracts a penalty of RMB 2,000, or RMB 2,000-RMB 10,000 for serious circumstances; in addition, a daily late-payment surcharge accrues at 0.05% on every overdue yuan of tax. Deliberate under-declaration or fraudulent tax evasion is penalised under Article 63 of the Tax Collection Administration Law: 50%-500% of the underpaid tax plus interest, with criminal prosecution under PRC Criminal Law Art. 201 (fines, asset seizure, and imprisonment up to 7 years). Failure to withhold on outbound dividends attracts a penalty of 50%-300% of the un-withheld amount under Article 69 of the Tax Collection Administration Law. Directors and the legal representative may be jointly liable for the entity's tax debts where the corporate veil is pierced, and exit bans are routinely imposed.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% statutory withholding tax on outbound dividends paid by a Chinese WFOE to a non-resident enterprise shareholder under PRC EIT Law Article 37 and Implementation Regulation Article 91, reduced to 5% under the China-HK Double Taxation Arrangement when the Hong Kong shareholder is the beneficial owner of the dividend and directly holds at least 25% of the capital of the WFOE at the time of distribution.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To obtain the 5% treaty withholding rate, the Hong Kong shareholder must submit a non-resident tax treaty benefit application to the State Taxation Administration (in practice through the distributing WFOE's competent tax bureau). The applicant must provide: (i) a valid Hong Kong Tax Residency Certificate issued by the Inland Revenue Department for the calendar year concerned; (ii) a completed beneficial ownership/income entitlement statement confirming the Hong Kong company has the right to control, use and enjoy the dividends and is not a mere conduit or agent; (iii) documentary evidence of direct equity ownership of at least 25% (shareholding register, company certificate, capital contribution records, and shareholder resolution); (iv) evidence of actual economic substance in Hong Kong such as office premises, business registration, employees, financial records, and board minutes; and (v) either a pre-approval from the tax authority or a subsequent refund application (Article 34 of the Tax Collection Administration Law) if the 10% was withheld pending verification. The tax authority may also apply the anti-abuse provisions of SAT Announcement No. 9 (2018) to deny benefits where the Hong Kong entity lacks substance, even if formal TRC and ownership documents are presented.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Chinese WHT on royalties and interest paid to a non-resident is 10% each (EIT Law and Implementation Regulation Art. 91). Under the China-HK DTA, the WHT is reduced to 7% for both royalties and interest, provided the Hong Kong payee is the beneficial owner and satisfies the treaty relief filing. Royalties for the use of EdTech copyrighted software, mobile applications, and branded content are treated as royalty income under Article 12 of the DTA. Interest paid on intercompany loans is further restrained by the arm's-length and thin capitalisation rules (EIT Law Art. 46), which may recharacterise excessive interest as a deemed dividend subject to dividend WHT.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Contemporaneous Local File thresholds under SAT Announcement No. 42 (2016): annual related-party tangible-asset transfers equal to or exceeding RMB 200 million; intangible-asset transfers equal to or exceeding RMB 100 million; financial-asset transfers equal to or exceeding RMB 100 million; and related-party services (including royalty and management fees) equal to or exceeding RMB 40 million. Master File preparation is mandatory when the aggregate amount of all related-party transactions equals or exceeds RMB 1 billion in the annual financial year. A Country-by-Country Report is required for a multinational group whose consolidated global annual revenue is at least RMB 5.5 billion in the preceding fiscal year.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Although China does not have a formal Economic Substance Regulation comparable to offshore jurisdictions, the PRC enforces substance-over-form through the General Anti-Avoidance Rule under EIT Law Article 47 and Article 112 of the Implementing Regulations. A WFOE must demonstrate real business operations, decision-making, employees, and risk-bearing functions that correspond to its EdTech income-generating activities (content production, platform maintenance, user support, and subscription pricing). In the cross-border context, a Hong Kong shareholder claiming the benefit of the China-HK DTA must prove economic substance in Hong Kong under the beneficial ownership test of SAT Announcement No. 9 (2018): it must possess legal and economic control over dividends, royalties, and interest, and its functions, assets, and risks cannot be absorbed by the Chinese WFOE. Pure shell arrangements, mailbox companies, or entities whose only activity is to receive Chinese-sourced income will be denied treaty relief and re-attributed as taxable in China.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Profit Shifting / Tax Evasion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE overpays royalties, management fees, technical service fees, or interest to the Hong Kong parent without any actual service provision, IP benefits, or risk control, intentionally converting Chinese operating profit into deductible cross-border payments and reducing the 25% EIT liability to near zero. The arrangement is documented with backdated agreements and circular invoices.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under PRC EIT Law Article 41 and Article 48, the SAT may make a discretionary transfer pricing adjustment and impose late interest on the underpaid tax. Article 63 of the Tax Collection Administration Law penalises fraudulent tax evasion with 50%-500% of the underpaid tax. Where the evaded tax amount is substantial (generally exceeding RMB 50,000 and 10% of the tax payable), PRC Criminal Law Article 201 imposes criminal liability: fines, seizure of property, and imprisonment for up to 7 years for the natural persons involved.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil will be pierced under PRC Company Law Article 20(3) if the directors or shareholders abuse the limited liability structure to evade taxes or commit fraud. Directors, the legal representative, and the CFO may be jointly and severally liable for the unpaid tax and penalties from their personal assets. The court may impose an exit ban (travel restriction), blacklist the individual in the tax enforcement system, and pursue criminal proceedings that can result in 3 to 7 years' imprisonment, with restitution of the full underpaid amount.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding Tax Failure and DTA Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE distributes dividends, royalties, or interest to Hong Kong related parties without withholding the statutory WHT, or the Hong Kong recipient is a mailbox company with no employees, office, or decision-making infrastructure, fraudulently claiming the 5% dividend treaty or 7% royalty/interest treaty rates merely because it has a Hong Kong Business Registration Certificate and Tax Residency Certificate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: EIT Law Articles 37 and 39 require the WFOE as withholding agent to withhold and remit the tax within 15 days of the cross-border payment. Failure to withhold triggers a penalty of 50%-300% of the un-withheld amount under Article 69 of the Tax Collection Administration Law, plus the required tax itself and daily surcharges. If treaty benefit is obtained by false declarations, the SAT will revoke the relief, impose the 10% statutory WHT differential, add late penalties, and proceed under criminal provisions where fraudulent intent is proven.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly approve cash distributions or cross-border payments without withholding, or who counsel the creation of a shell Hong Kong entity for treaty shopping, become personally responsible for the withheld tax, penalties, and interest as guaranty or joint liability under the veil-piercing rules. Their personal bank accounts may be frozen, travel bans imposed, and they are exposed to prosecution under PRC Criminal Law Art. 201 and Art. 195 (fraud), leading to imprisonment up to 7 years and confiscation of assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE or its Hong Kong parent holds itself out as a valid operating company but in fact has no physical premises, no substantive employees, no independent financial accounts, no board decision-making, and no operational control in Hong Kong. The entity functions solely as an invoice conduit for in-app subscription proceeds and royalty payments, with no observable Commercial Activity, despite claiming treaty benefits and low-risk classification in tax filings.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The SAT invokes the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (EIT Law Article 47) to disregard the shell entity, re-characterise the arrangement, and assess the true taxable owner in China. All treaty benefits are denied under SAT Announcement No. 9 (2018), and the WFOE is subject to additional 10% WHT on payments plus interest. In serious cases, Article 63 of the Tax Collection Administration Law applies, yielding a 50%-500% penalty; under the PRC Anti-Money Laundering Law, the shell arrangement may be treated as disguising the origin of taxable profits, leading to administrative fines and account freezes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil is pierced because the separate legal personality is abused to obstruct tax claims, making directors and the beneficial owner personally liable for all unpaid corporate tax, penalties, and interest. Courts may order personal asset attachment, travel bans, and criminal sanctions for tax evasion and money laundering (PRC Criminal Law Art. 191) with imprisonment up to 10 years. Directors are additionally barred from holding any director or senior management position and their personal foreign assets may be subject to cross-border enforcement under judicial assistance agreements.
